chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Salim, and Murazim, and Shuayb, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), from the man performing Tamattu':

when the night of Arafah enters, he circumambulates and performs Sa'ee, then he frees himself (from Ihram), then he enters Ihram again and goes to Mina. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem.'

key_terms.الْمُتَمَتِّعِ: The pilgrim performing Hajj al-Tamattu' (combining Umrah and Hajj)
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no problem / It is permissible
key_terms.لَيْلَةَ عَرَفَةَ: The night of Arafah, a key temporal marker in Hajj rituals
key_terms.يَحِلُّ: He frees himself from the state of Ihram (Hill)
key_terms.يَسْعَى: He performs Sa'ee (walking between Safa and Marwah)
key_terms.يَطُوفُ: He performs Tawaf (circumambulation of the Kaaba)
key_terms.يُحْرِمُ: He enters the state of Ihram again

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to free oneself from Ihram before the night of Arafah during Hajj al-Tamattu'?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the flexibility in the timing of the Hajj al-Tamattu' ritual, confirming that performing the Tawaf and Sa'ee and subsequently releasing oneself from Ihram before the night of Arafah is valid. The Imam’s response of 'La ba'sa' (no objection) underscores the permissibility of this sequence, distinguishing it from stricter interpretations that might require waiting until after the Day of Arafah. This ruling provides practical guidance for pilgrims managing the logistical flow of rites during the sacred days of Dhu al-Hijjah.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Salim, and Murazim, and Shuayb, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws about the man performing Tumatto
, and the night of Arafaat enters, so he circumambulates, and performs Sa’ee, then he frees (from Ihraam), and he goes to Mina. Heasws said: ‘There is no problem’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hisham ibn Salim and Murazim and Shu’ayb who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who enters Makkah in the night of ‘ Arafah, performs Tawaf and Sa‘y between al-Safa’ and al-Marwah, then comes out of the state of Ihram, then assumes the state of Ihram and goes to Mina’. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not harmful.’”
